args.body:
CLASSIFIED DEVIATION REPORT — MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT REDLINE
Prepared for: Northgale Systems, Inc. (the "Customer" / "client")
Counterparty: Corvid Analytics LLC (the "Provider" / "counterparty")
Base document: Northgale Systems client-form Master Services Agreement, v2 (execution-ready base)
Counterparty markup: Corvid Analytics LLC rev B counter-draft, transmitted by Dahlgren & Pike LLP, 9 July 2026 (operative)
Cross-reference materials: Northgale Commercial Contracting Playbook, 2026 Edition (the "Playbook"); engagement instruction letters of 14 July 2026 and 21 July 2026; superseded rev A transmittal of 26 June 2026 (retained for history only)
Prepared by: Harrow & Vane LLP
Date: [as of the engagement]

------------------------------------------------------------------
1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
------------------------------------------------------------------
We have compared the counterparty's operative rev B markup (the "Redline") against the executed client-form Master Services Agreement ("MSA") and cross-referenced each deviation against the 2026 Commercial Contracting Playbook (our contracting policies) and the governing correspondence. The Redline introduces eight (8) discrete changes. We classify all eight as deviations requiring response. Six (6) of the eight are out-of-policy under the Playbook and require escalation to the stated approver before any concession; two are out-of-policy deviations that can be countered at an approved fallback or rejected outright.

None of the counterparty's asks is consistent with the approved standard positions in the Playbook. Every change shifts risk to the Customer (higher fees, longer notice, additional suspension and wind-down rights, narrower liability exposure, and inferior service credits). We recommend rejecting the majority, countering two at approved fallback positions, and escalating the renewal-period and carve-out deletions to the Chief Legal Officer (and, for carve-out deletion, jointly with the CFO) consistent with the Playbook.

------------------------------------------------------------------
2. SCOPE AND METHODOLOGY
------------------------------------------------------------------
We reviewed, in full:
- MSA (executed client-form base), which sets the benchmark terms.
- The counterparty's rev B Redline (operative counter-draft of 9 July 2026), the only operative markup; rev A (26 June 2026) was withdrawn and disregarded.
- The 2026 Commercial Contracting Playbook, which governs standard positions, approved fallbacks, and escalation triggers for vendor-side services agreements where Northgale is the customer.
- The engagement instruction letters of 14 July 2026 and 21 July 2026 (governing instructions; the 21 July letter controls where it conflicts).

For each deviation we state: (a) the MSA/benchmark term; (b) the counterparty's requested change; (c) the applicable Playbook position/fallback/escalation rule; (d) the classification; and (e) the recommended response. Financial exposure for out-of-policy items is quantified at the $85,000 monthly base fee as the Playbook directs.

------------------------------------------------------------------
3. CLASSIFIED DEVIATION ANALYSIS
------------------------------------------------------------------
Classification legend: [A] Out-of-policy — escalate to stated approver; [B] Out-of-policy — rebut/reject; [C] Within approved fallback — counter; [D] Acceptable as drafted.

DEVIATION 1 — Section 2.2 (Renewal)
Benchmark (MSA): Automatic renewal in successive one (1) year renewal periods.
Counterparty Redline: Automatic renewal in successive two (2) year renewal periods (rationale: capacity planning).
Playbook (PB-1): Standard = one (1) year renewal periods; Approved fallback: NONE — multi-year renewal periods of any length are out of policy and require Chief Legal Officer (CLO) approval.
Classification: [A] Out-of-policy; multi-year renewal — escalation required.
Recommended response: REJECT. The counterparty's requested two-year renewal is out of policy. No approved fallback exists. Escalate to the CLO for any concession; absent CLO approval, hold the one-year standard renewal.
Exposure note: Multi-year renewal would lock the Customer into the full monthly run-rate for the added commitment without a corresponding benefit; quantify above standard if considered.

DEVIATION 2 — Section 4.3 (Late Amounts)
Benchmark (MSA): Late undisputed amounts accrue interest at 1.0% per month (or the lower maximum lawful rate).
Counterparty Redline: 1.5% per month.
Playbook (PB-4): Late interest never above 1.0% per month.
Classification: [B] Out-of-policy — rebut/reject.
Recommended response: REJECT and hold at 1.0% per month. The requested 1.5% exceeds the hard Playbook ceiling and is not approvable as a standard position.

DEVIATION 3 — NEW Section 4.4 (Suspension of Services)
Benchmark (MSA): No suspension right for the Provider (the client form grants Provider no right to suspend Services for non-payment).
Counterparty Redline: Adds a right for Provider to suspend Services if any undisputed invoice remains unpaid fifteen (15) days after its due date, until past-due amounts are paid in full.
Playbook (PB-4): Suspension-of-services rights are out of policy unless preceded by at least thirty (30) days' written cure notice, and any suspension right of any kind requires CFO sign-off.
Classification: [B]/[A] Out-of-policy — rebut/reject; any concession requires CFO sign-off.
Recommended response: REJECT in the requested form. If a suspension right is unavoidable, counter to require at least thirty (30) days' written cure notice before any suspension, and obtain CFO sign-off. Do not accept a 15-day cure trigger.

DEVIATION 4 — Section 7.2 (Termination for Convenience)
Benchmark (MSA): Customer may terminate for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice. No wind-down right in base form.
Counterparty Redline: Ninety (90) days' prior written notice.
Playbook (PB-2): Standard = thirty (30) days' notice; Approved fallback: up to forty-five (45) days; any notice period above 45 days requires CLO approval.
Classification: [C]/[A] Above approved fallback — counter at fallback; escalation if above.
Recommended response: REJECT at 90 days. Counter at the approved fallback of forty-five (45) days. Any concession above 45 days (including the requested 90 days) requires CLO approval and should not be conceded without it.

DEVIATION 5 — NEW Section 7.4 (Wind-Down)
Benchmark (MSA): No wind-down period and no wind-down compensation in the base client form.
Counterparty Redline: Adds a sixty (60) day wind-down period upon any termination other than for the Provider's uncured material breach, during which the Customer pays the full monthly base service fee plus all committed third-party costs.
Playbook (PB-3): A post-termination wind-down is acceptable only if (i) capped at thirty (30) days and (ii) compensation is limited to documented out-of-pocket costs and non-cancelable third-party commitments. Full-fee wind-down compensation is out of policy.
Classification: [A] Out-of-policy — escalation/rebut.
Recommended response: REJECT the full-fee 60-day wind-down. If any wind-down is conceded, counter to (i) a maximum of thirty (30) days and (ii) compensation limited to documented out-of-pocket costs and non-cancelable third-party commitments. Full-fee wind-down compensation is out of policy and non-concessible.

DEVIATION 6 — Section 9.1 (Limitation of Liability Cap Measurement Period)
Benchmark (MSA): Aggregate liability cap measured at the Fees paid or payable in the twenty-four (24) months preceding the first event giving rise to liability.
Counterparty Redline: Twelve (12) month measurement period.
Playbook (PB-5): Standard = twenty-four (24) months; Approved fallback floor = eighteen (18) months; a twelve (12) month measurement period is below the fallback floor and requires CLO approval.
Classification: [C]/[A] Below approved fallback floor — counter at fallback; escalation if below.
Recommended response: REJECT the 12-month period. Counter at the approved fallback floor of eighteen (18) months. The requested 12-month period is below the floor and may only be conceded with CLO approval.
Exposure note: At the $85,000 monthly base fee, the liability cap for a 12-month measurement = $1,020,000; at the 18-month approved fallback floor = $1,530,000; at the 24-month standard = $2,040,000. The counterparty's ask would reduce our recovered-caps exposure by roughly 50% against the standard.

DEVIATION 7 — Section 9.2 (Liability Cap Carve-Outs)
Benchmark (MSA): Cap does not apply to (a) breach of confidentiality; (b) Provider's IP indemnification; or (c) gross negligence/willful misconduct.
Counterparty Redline: Deletes clause (c), so gross negligence and willful misconduct become subject to the Section 9.1 cap. Clauses (a) and (b) retained.
Playbook (PB-5): The carve-outs for confidentiality, IP indemnification, and gross negligence/willful misconduct are non-negotiable; deletion of any carve-out requires joint CLO and CFO approval.
Classification: [A] Out-of-policy — non-negotiable carve-out — escalation required.
Recommended response: REJECT. The gross-negligence/willful-misconduct carve-out is a non-negotiable Playbook term. Any deletion requires joint CLO and CFO approval, which should not be sought as a routine matter. Hold all three carve-outs.

DEVIATION 8 — Section 11.2 (Service Credit Cap)
Benchmark (MSA): Aggregate service-credit cap of 20% of the monthly base service fee per month.
Counterparty Redline: Aggregate cap reduced to 10% of the monthly base service fee per month.
Playbook (PB-6): Standard = 20%; Approved fallback floor = 15%; a 10% aggregate credit cap is out of policy.
Classification: [B]/[C] Out-of-policy — rebut; counter at standard or fallback floor.
Recommended response: REJECT at 10%. Counter at the standard 20%, or at minimum the approved fallback floor of 15%. A 10% cap is out of policy and non-concessible without escalation.

------------------------------------------------------------------
4. QUANTIFIED EXPOSURE (at $85,000 monthly base fee)
------------------------------------------------------------------
Per the Playbook drafting note, escalation memos quantify exposure at the current monthly run-rate. Material quantified items:
- Liability cap (Section 9.1): 12-month (requested) = $1,020,000; 18-month (fallback floor) = $1,530,000; 24-month (standard) = $2,040,000. The requested change would cut the Customer-facing cap recovery by ~50%.
- Wind-down (Section 7.4, if conceded): 60-day full-fee wind-down ≈ $170,000 (two months at $85,000) plus committed third-party costs, versus a compliant 30-day out-of-pocket wind-down at a fraction of that amount.
- Renewal (Section 2.2, if conceded): converts the 1-year auto-renew to a 2-year commitment, adding a full extra year at $85,000/month = $1,020,000 of incremental locked-in exposure absent CLO approval.
- Interest (Section 4.3): an extra 0.5% per month on late amounts is a direct cost migration to the Customer.
All other changes (suspension, convenience notice, credit cap) reduce Customer flexibility or security without an offsetting benefit.

------------------------------------------------------------------
5. RECOMMENDED RESPONSES AND NEGOTIATION POSTURE
------------------------------------------------------------------
Recommended disposition by deviation:
1. Section 2.2 (renewal) — REJECT; escalate to CLO if the counterparty insists (no approved fallback).
2. Section 4.3 (late interest) — REJECT; hold at 1.0%.
3. Section 4.4 (suspension) — REJECT as drafted; if necessary counter with 30-day written cure and obtain CFO sign-off.
4. Section 7.2 (convenience) — REJECT at 90 days; counter at 45 days (approved fallback); escalate if above.
5. Section 7.4 (wind-down) — REJECT full-fee 60-day; counter to 30-day, out-of-pocket costs only.
6. Section 9.1 (cap) — REJECT at 12 months; counter at 18 months (fallback floor).
7. Section 9.2 (carve-outs) — REJECT; non-negotiable; deletion requires joint CLO/CFO approval (not recommended).
8. Section 11.2 (credits) — REJECT at 10%; counter at 20% (standard) or 15% (fallback floor).

The counterparty's rev A transmittal (26 June 2026) was withdrawn on 9 July 2026 and is superseded; no response positions are taken from rev A, and no rev A deliverable naming should be used.

------------------------------------------------------------------
6. APPROVALS / ESCALATION MATRIX
------------------------------------------------------------------
- CLO approval required for: renewal-period change (PB-1); convenience-notice above 45 days (PB-2); 12-month cap measurement (PB-5 under CLO).
- Joint CLO and CFO approval required for: any deletion of a Section 9.2 carve-out (PB-5).
- CFO sign-off required for: any suspension-of-services right (PB-4).
Where a requested concession lies with an approver specified above, no final position should be taken until that approval is documented. We recommend routing the out-of-policy asks (renewal and carve-out, at minimum) to the Deal Committee/Board approval package under the governing engagement instructions.

------------------------------------------------------------------
7. CONCLUSION
------------------------------------------------------------------
All eight counterparty changes in the rev B Redline constitute deviations from the executed MSA. Six are out-of-policy and require escalation or rebuttal; two can be countered at approved fallback positions.
